cells.tense: The letting go has its shape now and your hands are steady in it.
cells.act: let an exchange flow both ways
cells.ask: Take what is being handed back — the rest, the help, the credit — and keep it, with no return gesture ready.
cells.core:
You are past the part where you decide whether to let this finish. The date exists. Your attention goes to keeping the hours honest — the last message, the things to hand over, the loose account — and because your grip is loose, the ending keeps handing back parts of yourself you did not know were out on loan. That is not a reward, it is what a clean ending returns. The position holds without you.

Still, balance is an active thing, so keep one adjustment going. Take your own share for granted: something small, yours by right, taken without flinching and with nothing owed in return. Then the ending is an exchange rather than a bill you quietly pay alone.
cells.sheetLine: What is finishing is doing it with your full attention on it.
cells.verb: Letting what has finished finish, so what is arriving can arrive
cells.place: In the adjustment itself — adding here, subtracting there, hands on the balance while it moves

cells.tense: Every door still swinging toward its first day gets shoved shut by you before the week is out.
cells.act: stay in contact while it is hard
cells.ask: Stay a conversation past the point where you would normally end it — not to fix anything, just to remain where it is hard.
cells.core:
You are ending things ahead of their own pace. Plans get abandoned while they are still warm — nothing has failed, you have just found a wall before it had a chance to be a wall — and every clearing feels like freedom until the next one is needed, sooner each time. That is what makes the clearing tiring rather than clean.

One draw is marked for you. Stay in something a little past your quitting point, a conversation you would normally walk out on or put a wall across. Not forever, just past the hard part. Staying close to what is difficult, without your hand on the exit, is the practice that teaches your timing where the real edge is — and lets you find out how much of the ending was honest.

cells.tense: A room that emptied is still being kept tidy by you.
cells.act: go where the feeling is already pulling
cells.ask: Follow the pull you already feel past the point of thinking about it — walk toward it, and keep walking until that has decided.
cells.core:
There is a room in your life that emptied, and you still tend it. You are loyal to something that has stopped answering, and you set that down as steady; the effort of keeping it going is slow but it is not idle, and it uses time that has nowhere else to go. That is not a character flaw. It is a person standing at a threshold, deciding whether to cross.

The thing that would pull you across is not a grand ending; it is a direction — any one with an actual pull on you. Follow whatever already draws a little of your energy, past the point of only thinking about it. Direction is not decided, it is met, and the walking starts the rest.

cells.tense: A page turned weeks ago has not been noticed by the one who turned it.
cells.act: write the order things go in
cells.ask: Write out, from memory, the order of what changed recently in your life, and keep the page.
cells.core:
You have already let some things end. The problem is you have not been told, least of all by yourself — you keep handling what is left as though the arrangement were temporary. That is one of the ways a change this deep goes missing: nobody hands you a receipt, and the next task is more pressing than noticing.

So make the change visible. Write out the order of what happened, from memory, in plain steps, as an instruction to someone in your shoes. It is quick, and it forces the ending to exist somewhere outside you. Most of these pages take ten minutes and change nothing except the fact that the ending has been seen.
